description:
One S7-300 of the historian, chosen by $plc (only this family's PLCs; the fleet's table drills down to the page of each PLC's family): first its state — identity, CPU state, cycle, its paths, health loop, alerts — then what an S7-300 has: the diagnostic buffer, its mode changes, the faults recorded before STOP, the boots and the SZL answers (DB_PerfDiag layout 1); then the health loop, the cycle and the reads. Path-shaped panels follow the PLC's own paths (plc_registry.paths, $path). Trend panels switch to the 5 min / 1 h roll-ups on long ranges (raw 180 days, 5 min 2 years, 1 h forever). Data: the PLC historian (TimescaleDB). One definition rendered once per family. Alerts: this family's rules of rules-plc.yml, shown in the first section; as provisioned, nothing is sent.

GENERATED from the template maintainers' dashboard definitions (one for every PLC family) — do not edit it in this repository, a change is regenerated over; in your own copy, adapt it freely.

panels.description: The operating mode, DERIVED (plc_cpu_state()): DB_PerfDiag has no mode field on purpose, because OB1 — which would write it — does not run in STOP. RUN = the broker's CpuScanning verdict is true on an online path (its Seq heartbeat every 5 s; false after 10 s frozen: plc_state_change, as the Coreflux Hub shows it). UNREACHABLE = no path online (DeviceStatus stale or offline on every path of this PLC; Path status says which). Online but Seq frozen: STARTUP when the newest mode-transition entry of the diagnostic buffer (class 4, 0x43xx) entered STARTUP after the last record, or a boot stamped less than 5 min ago has no record yet; STOP — FAULT when an error OB recorded a fault after the last record (Faults recorded before STOP); else STOP (or HALT: the kit cannot tell them apart). The buffer cannot show a STOP while it lasts — its copy runs in OB1 — so its STOP entry appears after the restart (Mode changes, below). UNKNOWN = a path online but no CpuScanning verdict yet. NO DATA = the broker sends nothing for this PLC (no read, failed or not, in 90 s). Before the first verdict is stored, the state is derived from the reads: a frozen Seq is then proven by a successful PerfMon read that brought no new record.

targets.rawSql: SELECT plc_cpu_state('$plc') AS "CPU state"

panels.title: CPU state

panels.description: DeviceStatus on each path this PLC is read over (plc_registry.paths, one value per path, stacked), the broker's verdict (plc_state_change; plc_path_state()): ONLINE = a good read or Seq heartbeat on that path within 20 s, STALE up to 90 s, OFFLINE beyond. With two paths, one OFFLINE and the other ONLINE locates the fault: e.g. MPI = NetLink or MPI bus, PN = PN port or switch; all OFFLINE = CPU power, the shared LAN or the machine running the broker. With one path the table collapses: the path fails, cause unknown. NO DATA = the broker sends nothing. Before the first verdict is stored: a read without error in the last 90 s. Alerts plc_path_down (two or more paths), plc_unreachable (90 s).

targets.rawSql: SELECT u.via AS "path", plc_path_state('$plc', u.via) AS "state" FROM unnest(plc_paths('$plc')) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(via, i) ORDER BY u.i

panels.title: Path status

panels.description: The broker's CpuScanning verdict on an online path (plc_state_change; plc_scanning()): SCANNING = Seq moved within 10 s; NOT SCANNING = the path answers but Seq is frozen: the CPU is in STOP or HALT, the cause under Diagnostics (the key signal). UNKNOWN = no path online, or no verdict yet. Before the first verdict is stored: a successful PerfMon read in 90 s that brought no new record = NOT SCANNING. Alert plc_not_scanning.

targets.rawSql: SELECT plc_scanning('$plc') AS "CpuScanning"

panels.title: CPU scanning

panels.description: Each path's DB_PerfHealth slot as the PLC sees it, one value per path, stacked, the broker's verdict (plc_state_change; plc_health_state()): OK = Life confirmed; STALLED = the broker stopped echoing Life on that path while reads may look healthy (write refused, or the echo action died); CORRUPT = BadEcho rose: a second writer, a replay or a wrong address; NOT JUDGED = the CPU is not scanning (the loop runs in OB1: Life, Age_s and Healthy are frozen in STOP and prove nothing) or no path is online. Before the first verdict is stored: the newest row of the last 90 s (Age_s ≤ 15 s = OK). Alerts plc_health_stalled, plc_health_corrupt.

targets.rawSql: SELECT u.via AS "slot", plc_health_state('$plc', u.via) AS "state" FROM unnest(plc_paths('$plc')) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(via, i) ORDER BY u.i

panels.title: Health loop

panels.description: BootDate/BootTime of the newest boot DB_PerfMon reported (the startup OB stamps it, by the CPU's clock). A boot you did not expect: Boots and how they ended says how the previous one ended.

targets.rawSql: SELECT extract(epoch FROM max(ts_boot)) * 1000 AS "Last boot" FROM plc_boot WHERE plc_id = '$plc'

panels.title: Last boot

panels.description: DB_PerfMon records missing in the time range: Seq gaps within one boot, i.e. a reader outage longer than the ring (120 records = 2 min at a 1 s window). Exact to the record, over the raw records (kept 180 days); the gaps are listed under Reads. Alert plc_records_lost.

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(sum(missing), 0) AS "lost" FROM (SELECT boot_date, boot_time, seq AS gap_after, next_seq - seq - 1 AS missing FROM (SELECT boot_date, boot_time, seq, lead(seq) OVER (PARTITION BY boot_date, boot_time ORDER BY seq) AS next_seq FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts_plc)) s WHERE next_seq - seq > 1) g

panels.title: Records lost

panels.description: What this PLC is. Model, family, area, the paths it is read over and the watchdog (its maximum cycle time) from plc_registry and plc_model. From the newest DB_PerfDiag read (OB1 copies it once per boot): order number (SZL 0x0111 index 1), firmware (0x0111 index 7, decoded by plc_firmware(); the raw hex if the record has another shape), serial number (0x011C index 5) and station name (0x011C index 1).

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.model AS "model", coalesce(r.family, m.family) AS "family", r.area AS "area", array_to_string(r.paths, ' + ') AS "paths", coalesce(s.order_no, r.order_no) AS "order number", plc_firmware_of(r.plc_id) AS "firmware", plc_watchdog_ms('$plc') AS "watchdog", s.serial AS "serial", s.station AS "station" FROM plc_registry r LEFT JOIN plc_model m ON m.model = r.model LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT * FROM plc_diag_state d WHERE d.plc_id = r.plc_id AND d.order_no IS NOT NULL AND d.ts > now() - interval '30 days' ORDER BY d.ts DESC LIMIT 1) s ON true WHERE r.plc_id = '$plc'

panels.title: PLC identity

panels.description: The newest DB_PerfMon window (1 s): the average OB1 cycle. Frozen at the last window while the CPU is not in RUN (CPU state). Trend and histogram: Cycle.

targets.rawSql: SELECT cyc_avg_ms AS "avg" FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND ts_plc > now() - interval '2 days' ORDER BY ts_plc DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Cycle avg now

panels.description: The newest DB_PerfMon window (1 s): the longest OB1 cycle in it. Its share of the watchdog: the next tile. Frozen at the last window while the CPU is not in RUN.

targets.rawSql: SELECT cyc_max_ms AS "max" FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND ts_plc > now() - interval '2 days' ORDER BY ts_plc DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Cycle max now

panels.description: The longest cycle of the newest window as a share of this PLC's watchdog: yellow from 50 %, red from 80 % (alert plc_cycle_max_high at 80 % over 5 min). The watchdog is this PLC's maximum cycle time: plc_registry.watchdog_ms, else its model's preset (plc_model; 150 ms on the S7-300 and S7-1500), plc_watchdog_ms().

targets.rawSql: SELECT round((cyc_max_ms / plc_watchdog_ms('$plc') * 100)::numeric, 1) AS "of watchdog" FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND ts_plc > now() - interval '2 days' ORDER BY ts_plc DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Now % watchdog

panels.description: The longest cycle since the current boot, over its records (the boot the historian stored last: plc_boot.first_seen). Not DB_PerfMon's LifeMax header field: plc_ingest does not store it. The shortest cycle per window is in Cycle (410). A boot older than the raw retention (180 days) shows its retained part only.

targets.rawSql: SELECT max(c.cyc_max_ms) AS "max" FROM plc_cycle c JOIN (SELECT boot_date, boot_time, ts_boot FROM plc_boot WHERE plc_id = '$plc' ORDER BY first_seen DESC NULLS LAST, boot_date DESC, boot_time DESC LIMIT 1) b USING (boot_date, boot_time) WHERE c.plc_id = '$plc' AND c.ts_plc >= coalesce(b.ts_boot, '-infinity') - interval '1 day'

panels.title: Cycle max boot

panels.description: The longest cycle since the current boot as a share of this PLC's watchdog: yellow from 50 %, red from 80 %. The watchdog is this PLC's maximum cycle time: plc_registry.watchdog_ms, else its model's preset (plc_model; 150 ms on the S7-300 and S7-1500), plc_watchdog_ms().

targets.rawSql: SELECT round((max(c.cyc_max_ms) / plc_watchdog_ms('$plc') * 100)::numeric, 1) AS "of watchdog" FROM plc_cycle c JOIN (SELECT boot_date, boot_time, ts_boot FROM plc_boot WHERE plc_id = '$plc' ORDER BY first_seen DESC NULLS LAST, boot_date DESC, boot_time DESC LIMIT 1) b USING (boot_date, boot_time) WHERE c.plc_id = '$plc' AND c.ts_plc >= coalesce(b.ts_boot, '-infinity') - interval '1 day'

panels.title: Boot % watchdog

panels.description: Read time − PLC stamp, the smallest over the records that arrived in the last 10 min: the newest record of a read is at most one window old, so this is the CPU clock's offset, expected at 0–1 s. Hours = the CPU clock is not on UTC (set it, or plc_registry.clock_zone; an S7-1500's RD_SYS_T is UTC). Alert plc_clock_skew at ±10 s; trend under Health loop.

targets.rawSql: SELECT min(extract(epoch FROM ts_received - ts_plc)) AS "skew" FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND ts_plc > now() - interval '2 days' AND ts_received > now() - interval '10 minutes'

panels.title: Clock skew

panels.description: The newest class-4 entries of the diagnostic buffer (mode transitions and STOP causes, 0x43xx), whatever the time range. `entered` = the operating mode the entry names as requested (low nibble of byte 3 when the priority byte is 0xFF: 4 STOP, 6 STARTUP, 8 RUN, as TIA decodes them). The full buffer: Diagnostics.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts_plc AS "PLC stamp", event_hex AS "event id", coalesce(text, '(no text for this ID)') AS "text", cause_hex AS "STOP cause", CASE WHEN lower(substr(entry_hex, 5, 2)) = 'ff' THEN CASE substr(entry_hex, 8, 1) WHEN '4' THEN 'STOP' WHEN '6' THEN 'STARTUP' WHEN '8' THEN 'RUN' ELSE 'mode ' || substr(entry_hex, 8, 1) END END AS "entered" FROM plc_diag_event_text WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND class = 4 ORDER BY ts_plc DESC LIMIT 6

panels.title: Mode changes — newest

panels.description: The S7-300 rules of rules-plc.yml (the ones that link to this page) with their current state, every S7-300 in the historian. As provisioned, the notification policy mutes every alert: the state shows here and nothing is sent. Each rule links to its panel here, with the PLC selected.
panels.title: PLC alerts — state on this Grafana

panels.description: Every change of CpuScanning, DeviceStatus and Health per path, as the broker published it to the UNS (plc_state_change, by the broker's clock, kept forever): when the CPU stopped scanning, when a path went stale and offline, when the health loop stalled, was corrupted or could not be judged (unknown: the CPU not scanning). `from` — = the first verdict after a broker start. This is what the tiles above show, with the time each change happened.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts AS "broker time", via AS "path", signal, coalesce(prev, '—') AS "from", value AS "to" FROM plc_state_change WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts) ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 200

panels.title: State changes — the broker's verdicts

panels.description: SZL 0x00A0, newest first, whatever the time range (the buffer holds the newest 10; a burst between two reads is lost to us, not to TIA). Text = Siemens' published event text (A5E02790053 §35) from the view plc_diag_event_text, an exact ID first, then the class 8/9 module form (mask 0xF0FF); no text = an ID the manual does not list. Class = bits 12–15, entering/leaving = bit 8. Path = which paths delivered it (plc_arrival, 7 days). STOP cause = info 1 of a STOP to STARTUP or a restart request (0x4301, 0x1381–0x138D): the event that stopped the CPU before, kept even after that entry has left the buffer's top 10.

targets.rawSql: SELECT e.ts_plc AS "PLC stamp", e.event_hex AS "event id", coalesce(e.text, '(no text for this ID)') AS "text", e.cause_hex AS "STOP cause", e.cause_text AS "cause text", e.class, e.state, e.priority, e.ob_nr AS "OB", (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT a.via, ' + ') FROM plc_arrival a WHERE a.plc_id = e.plc_id AND a.kind = 'diag' AND a.fact_key = e.event_id::text AND a.ts_plc = e.ts_plc) AS "path", e.entry_hex AS "entry" FROM plc_diag_event_text e WHERE e.plc_id = '$plc' AND e.ts_plc > now() - interval '90 days' ORDER BY e.ts_plc DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Diagnostic buffer — newest entries

panels.description: Each fault an error OB (80/82/86) recorded in DB_PerfDiag before it stopped the CPU — count, then STOP: the most valuable fact the kit produces. Whatever the time range; kept forever. Alert plc_fault_event also counts OB80 calls (Cycle, OB80 calls) and a new boot after a boot that ended with OB counts (Boots and how they ended).

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts_fault AS "PLC stamp", fault_ob AS "OB", '0x' || upper(to_hex(ev_class::integer)) AS "event class", '0x' || upper(to_hex(flt_id::integer)) AS "fault id" FROM plc_fault WHERE plc_id = '$plc' ORDER BY fault_date DESC, fault_time DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Faults recorded before STOP

panels.description: One row per boot (DB_PerfMon's boot id), newest first BY ARRIVAL: `first seen` = when the historian first stored the boot (empty for a boot stored before the historian kept that column; such boots follow, by their PLC stamp), so a boot stamped by a CPU clock that was not set yet (an S7-1500 starts at 2012-01-01) cannot hide the current one. Its end as the NEXT boot's startup OB kept it (DB_PerfDiag PrevBoot*): the last Seq and the error-OB totals of that boot (OB80/82/86). Empty end = the boot is the current one, or ended before the kit ran. Kept forever.

targets.rawSql: SELECT b.ts_boot AS "boot (PLC clock)", b.first_seen AS "first seen", b.restart_count AS "restarts", e.last_seq AS "last seq", e.ob80 AS "OB80", e.ob82 AS "OB82", e.ob86 AS "OB86", array_to_string(b.edges_ms, ' ') AS "edges ms" FROM plc_boot b LEFT JOIN plc_boot_end e USING (plc_id, boot_date, boot_time) WHERE b.plc_id = '$plc' ORDER BY b.first_seen DESC NULLS LAST, b.boot_date DESC, b.boot_time DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Boots and how they ended

panels.description: The newest DB_PerfDiag read (layout 1) per path. `ret per step` = the CPU's answer to each SZL request (0x0111, 0x011C, 0x0074, 0x0D91, 0x0132, 0x00A0 …): 0 is proven, anything else is what this CPU refuses. Identity from SZL 0x0111/0x011C, the same on every path; LEDs, module state, protection and connections are stored raw (hex).

targets.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT ON (via) ts AS "read", via AS "path", diag_seq, array_to_string(ret, ' ') AS "ret per step", order_no, coalesce(plc_firmware(firmware_hex), firmware_hex) AS "firmware", serial, station, led_count AS "LEDs", mod_count AS "modules" FROM plc_diag_state WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND via IN ($path) AND ts > now() - interval '1 day' ORDER BY via, ts DESC

panels.title: DB_PerfDiag state per path — SZL answers and identity

panels.description: Seconds since the PLC last saw its Life value echoed on that path, the max of every read, one line per path of this PLC. 0–1 = the circle closes, writes included. Rising while reads succeed = writes refused or the broker's echo action died. Alert plc_health_stalled at 15 s. Range-aware: raw below a 1 h interval, the 1 h roll-up beyond (raw kept 180 days, the roll-up forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval), slot AS metric, max(age_s) AS value FROM plc_health WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts) AND ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND slot IN ($path) GROUP BY 1, 2) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), slot AS metric, max(age_s_max) AS value FROM plc_health_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days')) AND slot IN ($path) GROUP BY 1, 2)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Confirmation age per path (Age_s)

panels.description: The PLC's own counters since boot, per path. Losses = times Age_s passed the limit (the PLC lost its reader, by its own clock: LastLoss*). Bad echo = a value that was neither the current nor the previous Life: a second writer, a replay, a wrong address. Alert plc_health_corrupt when bad echo rises. Range-aware: raw below a 1 h interval, the 1 h roll-up beyond (raw kept 180 days, the roll-up forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval), slot || ' losses' AS metric, max(losses) AS value FROM plc_health WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts) AND ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND slot IN ($path) GROUP BY 1, 2) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), slot || ' losses' AS metric, max(losses_max) AS value FROM plc_health_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days')) AND slot IN ($path) GROUP BY 1, 2) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval), slot || ' bad echo' AS metric, max(bad_echo) AS value FROM plc_health WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts) AND ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND slot IN ($path) GROUP BY 1, 2) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), slot || ' bad echo' AS metric, max(bad_echo_max) AS value FROM plc_health_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days')) AND slot IN ($path) GROUP BY 1, 2)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Losses and bad echoes per path

panels.description: Per bucket, the record that arrived soonest after its stamp: the CPU clock's offset plus at most one window. It trends the clock's drift and catches a clock that was reset. Alert plc_clock_skew beyond ±10 s. Range-aware: raw records below a 5 min interval, plc_cycle_5m below 1 h, plc_cycle_1h beyond (raw kept 180 days, 5 min 2 years, 1 h forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts_plc, $__interval), min(extract(epoch FROM ts_received - ts_plc)) AS "skew" FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts_plc) AND ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') GROUP BY 1) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), min(skew_min_s) AS "skew" FROM plc_cycle_5m WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days') GROUP BY 1) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), min(skew_min_s) AS "skew" FROM plc_cycle_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND NOT (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days')) GROUP BY 1)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Clock skew — read time minus PLC stamp

panels.description: plc_arrival: one row per fact per path (7-day retention, so a longer range counts the last 7 days), over the paths this PLC is read over. With every path up, every record and diagnostic entry is seen on each, byte-identical; `content differs` must stay 0. A few `not on every path` at the newest edge are records another path has not read yet; many = a path was down (Reads per path says which). A PLC read over one path has nothing to compare: one row says so.

targets.rawSql: WITH c AS (SELECT plc_paths('$plc') AS paths), f AS (SELECT kind, fact_key, ts_plc, count(DISTINCT via) AS vias, count(DISTINCT fact_hash) AS hashes FROM plc_arrival, c WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND via = ANY (c.paths) AND $__timeFilter(ts_plc) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3) SELECT * FROM ( (SELECT f.kind, count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.vias = cardinality(c.paths)) AS "on every path", count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.vias < cardinality(c.paths)) AS "not on every path", count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.hashes > 1) AS "content differs" FROM f, c WHERE cardinality(c.paths) > 1 GROUP BY f.kind) UNION ALL (SELECT 'one path (' || coalesce(array_to_string(c.paths, ''), '') || '): nothing to compare', NULL, NULL, NULL FROM c WHERE cardinality(c.paths) < 2)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Paths, the same facts

panels.description: From DB_PerfMon's ring: the CPU measures every OB1 cycle (1 ms resolution on an S7-300) and closes a record per window. Dashed line = 80 % of this PLC's watchdog (query B, drawn as a threshold, not a series). The watchdog is this PLC's maximum cycle time: plc_registry.watchdog_ms, else its model's preset (plc_model; 150 ms on the S7-300 and S7-1500), plc_watchdog_ms(). Alert plc_cycle_max_high. Range-aware: raw records below a 5 min interval, plc_cycle_5m below 1 h, plc_cycle_1h beyond (raw kept 180 days, 5 min 2 years, 1 h forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts_plc, $__interval), min(cyc_min_ms) AS "min", sum(cyc_avg_ms * cycles) / nullif(sum(cycles), 0) AS "avg", max(cyc_max_ms) AS "max" FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts_plc) AND ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') GROUP BY 1) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), min(cyc_min_ms) AS "min", sum(cyc_avg_ms * cycles) / nullif(sum(cycles), 0) AS "avg", max(cyc_max_ms) AS "max" FROM plc_cycle_5m WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days') GROUP BY 1) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), min(cyc_min_ms) AS "min", sum(cyc_avg_ms * cycles) / nullif(sum(cycles), 0) AS "avg", max(cyc_max_ms) AS "max" FROM plc_cycle_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND NOT (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days')) GROUP BY 1)) t ORDER BY 1
SELECT 0.8 * plc_watchdog_ms('$plc') AS "limit"

panels.title: Cycle time — min / avg / max per window

panels.description: OB1 cycles per second of PLC time. The inverse of the average cycle; a drop is load (or the minimum cycle time padding it). Range-aware: raw records below a 5 min interval, plc_cycle_5m below 1 h, plc_cycle_1h beyond (raw kept 180 days, 5 min 2 years, 1 h forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts_plc, $__interval), sum(cycles) * 1000.0 / nullif(sum(window_ms), 0) AS "cycles/s" FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts_plc) AND ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') GROUP BY 1) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), sum(cycles) * 1000.0 / nullif(sum(window_ms), 0) AS "cycles/s" FROM plc_cycle_5m WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days') GROUP BY 1) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), sum(cycles) * 1000.0 / nullif(sum(window_ms), 0) AS "cycles/s" FROM plc_cycle_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND NOT (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days')) GROUP BY 1)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Cycles per second

panels.description: Cycles per bucket in the newest record in the range (raw records, kept 180 days). Bucket edges are the ones the CPU booted with (plc_boot.edges_ms, set once per PLC before any comparison).

targets.rawSql: WITH e AS (SELECT edges_ms FROM plc_boot WHERE plc_id = '$plc' ORDER BY first_seen DESC NULLS LAST, boot_date DESC, boot_time DESC LIMIT 1), r AS (SELECT hist FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts_plc) ORDER BY ts_plc DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT CASE WHEN i = 1 THEN '< ' || e.edges_ms[1] WHEN i = 8 THEN '≥ ' || e.edges_ms[7] ELSE e.edges_ms[i - 1] || '–' || e.edges_ms[i] END || ' ms' AS bucket, r.hist[i] AS "cycles" FROM generate_series(1, 8) AS i CROSS JOIN r LEFT JOIN e ON true ORDER BY i

panels.title: Cycle-time histogram — newest window

panels.description: Every cycle in the range by bucket, log scale: the long tail is what matters. Percentiles are exact to the bucket. The edges are the current boot's; a range across a change of edges mixes them. Range-aware: raw records below a 5 min interval, plc_cycle_5m below 1 h, plc_cycle_1h beyond (raw kept 180 days, 5 min 2 years, 1 h forever).

targets.rawSql: WITH e AS (SELECT edges_ms FROM plc_boot WHERE plc_id = '$plc' ORDER BY first_seen DESC NULLS LAST, boot_date DESC, boot_time DESC LIMIT 1), h AS (SELECT i, sum(n) AS n FROM ( SELECT i, sum(hist[i]) AS n FROM plc_cycle, generate_series(1, 8) AS i WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts_plc) AND ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') GROUP BY i UNION ALL SELECT u.i, u.n FROM (SELECT ARRAY[sum(h0), sum(h1), sum(h2), sum(h3), sum(h4), sum(h5), sum(h6), sum(h7)] AS a FROM plc_cycle_5m WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days')) x, unnest(x.a) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(n, i) UNION ALL SELECT u.i, u.n FROM (SELECT ARRAY[sum(h0), sum(h1), sum(h2), sum(h3), sum(h4), sum(h5), sum(h6), sum(h7)] AS a FROM plc_cycle_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND NOT (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days'))) x, unnest(x.a) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(n, i)) s GROUP BY i) SELECT CASE WHEN h.i = 1 THEN '< ' || e.edges_ms[1] WHEN h.i = 8 THEN '≥ ' || e.edges_ms[7] ELSE e.edges_ms[h.i - 1] || '–' || e.edges_ms[h.i] END || ' ms' AS bucket, h.n AS "cycles" FROM h LEFT JOIN e ON true ORDER BY h.i

panels.title: Cycle-time histogram — summed over the range

panels.description: Per window from the ring. OB82/OB86 are counted per boot only (DB_PerfMon's header totals, kept by the startup OB: Boots and how they ended) — a per-window figure is not in the ring. Alert plc_fault_event (OB80 in the last 10 min). Range-aware: raw records below a 5 min interval, plc_cycle_5m below 1 h, plc_cycle_1h beyond (raw kept 180 days, 5 min 2 years, 1 h forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts_plc, $__interval), sum(ob80_cnt) AS "OB80 calls", count(*) FILTER (WHERE flags & 2 > 0) AS "windows with OB80 (bit 1)", count(*) FILTER (WHERE flags & 1 > 0) AS "first window after boot (bit 0)" FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts_plc) AND ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') GROUP BY 1) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), sum(ob80) AS "OB80 calls", sum(win_ob80) AS "windows with OB80 (bit 1)", sum(win_first) AS "first window after boot (bit 0)" FROM plc_cycle_5m WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days') GROUP BY 1) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), sum(ob80) AS "OB80 calls", sum(win_ob80) AS "windows with OB80 (bit 1)", sum(win_first) AS "first window after boot (bit 0)" FROM plc_cycle_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND NOT (NOT ($__interval_ms < 300000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND $__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '729 days')) GROUP BY 1)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: OB80 calls and window flags

panels.description: Ask → answer of each whole-DB read, as the broker's decoder timed it, per path of this PLC. Measured on the S7-300: DB_PerfMon 1.5 s over MPI, 0.3 s over PN. A rise on one path only = that path's link. Range-aware: raw below a 1 h interval, the 1 h roll-up beyond (raw kept 180 days, the roll-up forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval), via || ' / ' || db_name AS metric, avg(read_ms) AS value FROM plc_read WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts) AND ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND via IN ($path) AND error IS NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), via || ' / ' || db_name AS metric, sum(read_ms_avg * (reads - errors)) / nullif(sum(reads - errors), 0) AS value FROM plc_read_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days')) AND via IN ($path) GROUP BY 1, 2)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Read duration per path and DB

panels.description: What polling costs the link: every read's bytes over the bucket. Constant by design (fixed DBs, fixed rate) — keep it so across any comparison. Range-aware: raw below a 1 h interval, the 1 h roll-up beyond (raw kept 180 days, the roll-up forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval), via AS metric, sum(bytes) * 1000.0 / $__interval_ms AS value FROM plc_read WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts) AND ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND via IN ($path) GROUP BY 1, 2) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), via AS metric, sum(bytes) * 1000.0 / greatest($__interval_ms, 3600000) AS value FROM plc_read_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days')) AND via IN ($path) GROUP BY 1, 2)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Bytes read per second, per path

panels.description: Reads per bucket, split by outcome, per path of this PLC. A path whose `ok` line drops to zero while another carries on is a path fault (alert plc_path_down); every path = plc_unreachable. Range-aware: raw below a 1 h interval, the 1 h roll-up beyond (raw kept 180 days, the roll-up forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval), via || CASE WHEN error IS NULL THEN ' ok' ELSE ' failed' END AS metric, count(*) AS value FROM plc_read WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND via IN ($path) AND $__timeFilter(ts) AND ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') GROUP BY 1, 2) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), via || ' ok' AS metric, sum(reads - errors) AS value FROM plc_read_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND via IN ($path) AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days')) GROUP BY 1, 2) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), via || ' failed' AS metric, sum(errors) AS value FROM plc_read_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND via IN ($path) AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days')) GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING sum(errors) > 0)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Reads per path — ok and failed

panels.description: Slots the decoder refused per bucket. After a warm restart, 'newer than header' carries the previous boot's slots until they are overwritten; 'bad stamp' = a CPU clock value that is not a date. Empty slots are not shown. Range-aware: raw below a 1 h interval, the 1 h roll-up beyond (raw kept 180 days, the roll-up forever).

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM ((SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval), sum(rej_future) AS "newer than header", sum(rej_slot) AS "wrong slot", sum(rej_old) AS "about to be overwritten", sum(rej_stamp) AS "bad stamp" FROM plc_read WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts) AND ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days') AND via IN ($path) AND db_name = 'PerfMon' GROUP BY 1) UNION ALL (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(bucket, $__interval), sum(rej_future) AS "newer than header", sum(rej_slot) AS "wrong slot", sum(rej_old) AS "about to be overwritten", sum(rej_stamp) AS "bad stamp" FROM plc_read_1h WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND (NOT ($__interval_ms < 3600000 AND $__timeFrom() > now() - interval '179 days')) AND via IN ($path) AND db_name = 'PerfMon' GROUP BY 1)) t ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Records refused by the read contract

panels.description: The connector's or the decoder's own words. 'not connected' = the route lost the PLC on that path; 'layout' = a DB with another version or size than the decoder expects. Raw reads, kept 180 days.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts AS "time", via AS "path", db_name AS "DB", error, read_ms FROM plc_read WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND via IN ($path) AND error IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(ts) ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Failed reads — newest

panels.description: Each gap within one boot: the records after `after seq` that no read delivered, because the reader was gone for longer than the ring holds. Raw records, kept 180 days. Alert plc_records_lost.

targets.rawSql: SELECT boot_date || '/' || boot_time AS "boot", gap_after AS "after seq", missing FROM (SELECT boot_date, boot_time, seq AS gap_after, next_seq - seq - 1 AS missing FROM (SELECT boot_date, boot_time, seq, lead(seq) OVER (PARTITION BY boot_date, boot_time ORDER BY seq) AS next_seq FROM plc_cycle WHERE plc_id = '$plc' AND $__timeFilter(ts_plc)) s WHERE next_seq - seq > 1) g ORDER BY boot_date DESC, boot_time DESC, gap_after DESC LIMIT 50
